situation:
You are a young adult working your first full-time job and carrying a balance on your first credit card. A relative has just given you a cash gift. The insurance agent (judge) at ARDENWOOD MUTUAL INSURANCE has agreed to review your auto policy with you before it renews.

Raising the deductible on the auto policy would cut the premium you pay each month. Workers' compensation would cover an injury at work and your employer's plan would replace part of your wages, but Social Security covers only long disabilities, so an off-the-job injury would land on you. The relative gave the cash gift so you could open a retirement account.

Raising the deductible and putting the gift into a retirement account would start your savings early, but the gift would then be the only money available to cover the larger deductible after a collision and would come straight back out. Keeping the lower deductible and putting the gift toward the credit card balance clears the debt, though the higher premium keeps taking from every paycheck and nothing goes into a retirement account this year.

A coworker has suggested adding an old dent to a future claim to cover the deductible, which you know is insurance fraud. The insurance agent (judge) wants your recommendation on the deductible and the gift, and what you will do about the suggestion. The insurance agent (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the insurance agent (judge) at ARDENWOOD MUTUAL INSURANCE. The background is the same as the situation above.

You have agreed to review the auto policy before it renews and to hear whether the deductible should be raised with the gift going into a retirement account, or the lower deductible kept with the gift going toward the credit card balance, and what will be done about the coworker's suggestion.

You will greet the participant, ask to hear their ideas, and after the presentation you will ask the following questions:
